title: HC bucketization sensitivity snapshot — Q1 working
body:
Purpose:
Quick exploratory working note for an alternative headcount-bucketization approach to link hiring phasing with pricing sensitivity and GPU mix. Not a final model — thinking doc to surface tradeoffs and quick triggers for Q2 commit.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Proposal: group hiring into 3 operational buckets (Core serving, Optimization & Tooling, Customer Ops) tied to revenue buckets rather than FTE-by-role alone. This reduces marginal cost per token under mid/high batching regimes.
- Primary lever to test: 10–15% token price increase vs 15% price cut scenario and the implied headcount scale-back / scale-up by bucket.
- Quick actionable triggers at the bottom for product/sales/eng.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline token price: $0.0008 per token equivalent (mix of gen+embeds normalized).
- Baseline committed Dedicated capacity cost (monthly): $420k (multi-region reserve mix).
- Average hire fully loaded (eng SWE): $210k ARR run-rate (salary+burden+tools). Ops / RL / Solutions average: $160k.
- GPU mix baseline: 60% A100-like, 30% H100-like, 10% spot T4/lesser for inference experiments.
- Elasticity: for small-mid customers assume price elasticity -0.8; for large enterprise -0.25. (very rough)

Baseline budget snapshot (quarter view, simplified):
CSV-style table headers: bucket, FTE, avg-cost-per-FTE-annual, quarterly-cost, notes
Core serving, 18, $210,000, $945,000, runtime + infra + 24/7 SRE overlap
Optimization & Tooling, 6, $210,000, $315,000, batching/quant/compile work
Customer Ops & Sales engineering, 5, $160,000, $200,000, on-call support + onboarding
Total, 29, -, $1,460,000, excludes capitalized infra & cloud egress credits

Three scenarios (A/B/C):
A) Price UP +10% (conservative):
- Assumed demand shift: -5% churnable volume from smallest tier, +1% enterprise churn improvement. Net revenue +8.5% (approx).
- Hiring implication: delay 4 hires in Customer Ops and 2 in Optimization for one quarter; accelerate 2 Core serving hires to improve latency SLAs for expansion customers.
- Net quarter cash delta: +$120k (price) - saved hiring spend ~$220k (deferred) + marginal infra usage +$30k = net +$330k.

B) Price DOWN -15% (aggressive to win share):
- Assumed demand uplift: +22% volume from small-mid customers, enterprise stable or slight downgrade -1%. Unit revenue drops but token volume rises. Elasticity assumptions produce net revenue +2% or flat depending on mix.
- Hiring implication: need more Capacity (Core serving) headcount earlier (hire 6 more in serving), freeze Optimization hires. This increases quarterly payroll by ~$630k but may be partially offset by increased revenue and higher GPU utilization.

C) Neutral price, cost-shock (GPU spot price +25%):
- No price change but infra cost rises. We need to assess headcount trade (more SRE/Infra to optimize vs pass through costs). Suggest pause on non-critical customer engineering hires and move 2 hires from Customer Ops to a short-term Infra performance sprint.

Sensitivity matrix (simplified):
- Rows: Price change (-15%, 0%, +10%); Columns: Net payroll delta, infra delta, cash delta (quarter), recommended hr action
- Example cell: (-15%) => payroll +$630k, infra +$140k, cash delta -$180k, action: accelerate Core-serving hiring + temporary hiring freeze in tooling

Bucketization notes (why this is different):
- Instead of per-role permissioning, bucketize by function tied to revenue-generating surface area. This makes it easier to throttle or accelerate entire value chains (eg: if price cut focus is growth, accelerate Core; for margin focus, prioritize Optimization & Tooling).
- Allows simple rollback: furlough or slow-hire by bucket rather than role-by-role which reduces cross-team disruption.

Open operational triggers (draft):
- If net revenue change > +6% for 30 days -> release 2 Core-serving offers (immediate).
- If infra cost per token > 1.12x baseline for two consecutive weeks -> pause non-critical hires and route optimization sprint.
- If small-mid ARR cohort LTV drops by >8% post-price change after 60 days -> restore baseline pricing for that cohort.

To-dos & unanswered items (notes to self):
- TODO: run a finer Monte Carlo with 10k sims for elasticity across customer cohorts (link to model in repo).
- TODO: ask Product for expected latency SLAs if we accelerate Core-serving hires (Marta).
- Question: how do reserved GPU contract breakpoints change if we shift 10% of load to cloud-neutral fast paths? Need infra input (Ethan).

Quick links and provenance:
- Reference model: github:repo/cost-models/2026/hc-buckets-sim (WIP).
- Related Confluence: FIN-HC-BUCKETS-2026 (planning page).
- Jira tasks: FIN-4232 (sensitivity runs), FIN-4290 (pricing experiment), ENG-981 (batching perf uplift).

Appendix: rough burn math (quarter):
- Payroll baseline (quarter): $1.46M.
- Committed infra baseline (quarter, Dedicated + cloud overlay): $1.26M.
- Total baseline burn (quarter): $2.72M.
- Breakout: if we defer 6 hires (avg loaded $210k) for the quarter, payroll delta ~ -$315k.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact and exploratory. Please annotate the Confluence page with model outputs you want included in the next revision. If we pick scenario B for growth, we must align with Sales on expected conversion lift within 60 days or we risk margin bleed.

---
Working inline comments: (1) consider renaming Optimization & Tooling -> Inference Platform (broader). (2) We should maintain a separate tracker for capital GPU commit vs monthly cloud — linking to finance capex planning.

End of snapshot.
